formulas.formula: Every rent check and every repair, organized by property.
1. Properties: add up to 5 rentals with their monthly rent, value and the cash you put in.
2. Categories: these are ready to go (they follow IRS Schedule E). Rename or add your own; just give each one a kind.
3. Transactions: log every rent payment and every expense with its property and category.
4. Rent Roll shows who has paid each month. Monthly Summary and Property P&L show income, NOI and cash flow.
5. Tax Summary groups the year by Schedule E line for each property, ready for your tax preparer.
Net operating income = income minus operating expenses (before mortgage payments).
What's left after operating expenses, mortgage interest and principal, and improvements.
Income, Operating, Interest, Principal (pays down the loan; not deductible), CapEx (improvements, depreciated), Deposit (security deposits you hold; not income).
Log a deposit you return as a minus amount in Security Deposit.
Use Tax Summary as an organized starting point and confirm with a tax professional.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: paid in full, or positive cash flow.
Yellow: partial payment, or worth a look.
Red: unpaid, negative, or an entry to check.
Thank you for your purchase! Here's to steady rent and quiet tenants.

formulas.formula: All properties together, month by month. NOI = income − operating. Cash flow also takes off mortgage interest, principal and improvements.

section_bars.label: NOI AND CASH FLOW BY PROPERTY

formulas.formula: Each property for the year. Cap rate = NOI ÷ current value. Cash-on-cash = cash flow ÷ cash invested (both for the year so far).
The year by Schedule E line, for each property. A tidy starting point for your tax preparer (not tax advice). Depreciation isn't included.
